title: Section 26AH ITAA 1936 — bonuses on short-term life assurance policies
summary: Bonuses received under eligible life assurance policies are assessable within the 10-year eligible period — full amount in years 1-8, two-thirds in year 9, one-third in year 10. Eligible policy = life assurance policy with commencement of risk after 27 August 1982 (not a post-2002 funeral policy). Deemed receipt where bonuses are reinvested (unless surrender/maturity value increases); unit-value increases on unit-linked policies are deemed bonuses; death and illness benefits are excluded; a 25% premium increase restarts the eligible period. A 30% rebate applies under s 160AAB and CGT on surrender/maturity is disregarded to the extent s 26AH applies. Subsection coverage: operative 1,3,4,5,6,7,9,11,13 mapped to nodes; 2 (paid-up policy in lieu — deemed continuation) and 12 (sale/assignment — CGT disposal) noted as machinery; 6A (non-complying super fund) and 14 (pre-1983 transitional) out of scope for the standard investment-bond pattern.

nodes.label: You hold a life assurance policy and receive an amount under it as or by way of a bonus
nodes.body: Section 26AH taxes bonuses received under short-term life assurance policies ('eligible policies') within a 10-year eligible period. Amounts received after the 10th year are not assessable. A 30% rebate is available under s 160AAB.

statute.title: Bonuses and other amounts received in respect of certain short-term life assurance policies

cases.title: Russell Eryl Glenn and Rex William Over and Commissioner of Taxation

nodes.label: Is the policy an 'eligible policy'?
nodes.body: An eligible policy is a life assurance policy with a date of commencement of risk after 27 August 1982, other than a funeral policy (as defined in ITAA 1997) issued on or after 1 January 2003. If it is not an eligible policy, s 26AH does not apply at all.

nodes.label: Not an eligible policy — s 26AH does not apply (normal rules apply to the amount)
Was the amount received after 27 August 1982?
nodes.body: Section 26AH applies only to amounts received after 27 August 1982 under an eligible policy (s 26AH(3)).

nodes.label: Is the amount received as or by way of a bonus (or a unit-value increase on a unit-linked policy)?
nodes.body: The charging provision (s 26AH(6)) catches amounts received during the eligible period as or by way of a bonus that would otherwise not be assessable. For unit-linked policies, an increase in unit value is deemed to be a bonus (s 26AH(9)).

nodes.label: Was the amount received during the 10-year eligible period?
nodes.body: The eligible period is the period of 10 years commencing on the date of commencement of risk (s 26AH(1)). If received after the eligible period, the bonus is not assessable under s 26AH. Note the 25% premium rule (s 26AH(13)) can restart the eligible period.

nodes.label: Was the bonus actually paid to you, or reinvested/dealt with on your behalf?
nodes.body: A taxpayer is taken to have received an amount even if it is not actually paid but is reinvested or dealt with on their behalf or as directed (s 26AH(4)).

nodes.label: Did the reinvestment increase the amount expected on surrender or maturity?
nodes.body: Subsection (4) does not apply where the amount is reinvested so as to increase the amount that might reasonably be expected to be received on surrender or maturity (s 26AH(5)) — so bonuses merely credited and retained in the policy are not taxed during the policy's life.

nodes.label: Was the amount received in consequence of the death or illness of the insured person?
nodes.body: Subsection (6) does not apply to amounts received in consequence of the death or illness of the insured person (s 26AH(7)(a)).

nodes.label: Calculate the assessable portion of the bonus
nodes.body: Full amount assessable if received in the first 8 years; two-thirds if received in the 9th year; one-third if received in the 10th year (s 26AH(6)). A 30% tax rebate applies under s 160AAB. Capital gains on surrender/maturity are disregarded to the extent s 26AH applies (s 118-300 ITAA 1997).

statute.title: Rebate for amounts included in assessable income under s 26AH

nodes.label: Did premiums increase by more than 25% in any assurance year?
nodes.body: If the premiums payable in an assurance year exceed those of the immediately preceding year by more than 25%, the eligible period restarts from that year for certain purposes (s 26AH(13)) — a new 10-year clock begins and the bonus may again be assessable.

nodes.label: Bonus is assessable (with the s 160AAB 30% rebate); CGT on the policy is disregarded to that extent
nodes.body: The assessable portion is included in assessable income of the year received (s 26AH(6)). The s 160AAB rebate reduces the tax payable on it. On surrender or maturity, capital gains are disregarded to the extent s 26AH applied (s 118-300 ITAA 1997).

nodes.label: Bonus is not assessable under s 26AH
nodes.body: No amount is included in assessable income under s 26AH — the bonus is not taxed (or, if received in consequence of death or illness, it retains its normal character).

nodes.label: Complete — the bonus is either assessable (with rebate) or not assessable under s 26AH
Did you receive an advance or loan from the assurer at nil or below-arm's-length interest?
nodes.body: An advance or loan from the assurer (or another person at the assurer's request/agreement) on which interest is not payable, or is payable below the arm's length rate, is deemed to be an amount to which s 26AH(9)(a) applies — i.e. treated as a bonus received under a unit-linked policy (s 26AH(11)).
